summary: Pagan Creek Dike is a historic causeway in Lewes, Sussex County, Delaware, about 700 feet long and nine to ten feet wide at the top. It is built of clay and loam over a sand footing resting on marsh mud, and still stands about two feet above the adjacent marsh in places. Dated to the mid- to late-17th century, it is one of the oldest surviving road structures in Delaware and was apparently built by Dutch settlers to link the Dutch West India Company fort with the hinterland beyond Pagan Creek.
one_line: Pagan Creek Dike is a mid-to-late 17th-century causeway in Lewes, Delaware, possibly built by Dutch settlers to link their fort inland.
